subject: series

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Alexandre Dumas's beloved swashbuckling adventure with D'Artagnan and the Musketeers receives an illustrated adaptation faithful to the spirit of the original romance and action.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Louis Stevenson's classic pirate adventure receives the Marvel Illustrated treatment, with art that brings Long John Silver and Jim Hawkins to vivid illustrated life.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: An adaptation of James Fenimore Cooper's frontier classic, capturing the adventure and tragedy of the French and Indian War through accessible comics storytelling.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: An adaptation of Alexandre Dumas's swashbuckling historical adventure with classic illustration style, bringing the tale of a royal prisoner and the Musketeers to comics readers.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series

subject: series

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek and Jay Anacleto's sequel to the original Marvels revisits photographer Phil Sheldon as he faces mortality while reflecting on a lifetime witnessing the Marvel Universe's defining moments.
author: Kurt Busiek

subject: series
synopsis: Alex de Campi and Tony Parker's spy thriller following an American woman living in Britain in the 1960s who discovers her husband is a Russian sleeper agent — and is recruited by both sides simultaneously. Sharp Cold War espionage with strong period flavor.

subject: series
synopsis: An indie comedy series exploring absurdist scenarios and humor.

subject: series
synopsis: Ryan North and Shelli Paroline and Braden Lamb's sci-fi comedy featuring a ragtag spaceship crew discovering the body of King Midas and the universe-destroying golden touch still active on a distant planet. author: Ryan North

subject: series
synopsis: Bob Fingerman's slice-of-life autobiographical comic following Rob Hoffman, a young cartoonist in 1990s New York navigating the end of a bad marriage, friendships, and the unglamorous reality of trying to make a living making art. Funny, honest, and bracingly real.

subject: series
synopsis: Set in the universe of H.P. Lovecraft's Arkham, this series follows two women investigators at Miskatonic University who uncover the horrifying truth behind the institution's occult research. An honorable attempt to revive a genuinely important historical character.

subject: series
synopsis: A crime thriller set in London's underworld, following a hitman entangled in supernatural and criminal conspiracies.
author: Gary Erskine

subject: series
synopsis: Chelsea Cain's sharp, feminist, funny series about Bobbi Morse balancing S.H.I.E.L.D. missions with medical treatments, celebrated for its wit and the controversial #8 'feminist' cover. Cut short at 8 issues.
author: Chelsea Cain

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Seeley, Sarah Beattie and Rebekah Isaacs's sex comedy: underfunded scientists bankroll space exploration by filming their encounters with aliens for an online audience.

subject: series

author: Alan Zelenetz, Chris Warner

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire and Greg Smallwood's acclaimed Moon Knight, a fractured trip through Marc Spector's identities that begins in an asylum, followed by Max Bemis's Legacy run.
author: Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: Geoffrey Thorne's series following basketball star Morris Sackett gaining Inhuman powers that let him inhabit others' bodies, an ambitious take on identity and privilege that was cancelled before fully realizing its potential.
author: Geoffrey Thorne

subject: series
synopsis: John Lees and Ryan Lee's psychological horror miniseries about a family's camping trip that descends into surreal menace when an ominous presence begins exerting control. A slow-burn horror story with literary ambitions and striking visual design.
author: John Lees

subject: series
synopsis: David Hine's House of M tie-in exploring life in District X, the mutant ghetto of New York, during the altered reality.
author: David Hine

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series spinning out of the classic DC title, featuring new takes on Garbage Man, Robotman, and Tanga in three separate backup strips within each issue. An attempt to revive the anthology format for minor DC characters.

synopsis: Riichi Ueshiba's surreal romantic manga about a boy who accidentally tastes the drool of a strange new classmate and becomes addicted to it, creating a psychic bond between them. Strange, specific, and oddly sincere.
author: Riichi Ueshiba

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Parker and Tom Fowler's occult comedy follows an elegant but morally suspect magician named Mysterius and his new assistant as they investigate supernatural cases with an entertainingly irreverent tone.
author: Jeff Parker

subject: series
synopsis: Marjorie Liu's continuation of the NYX series following the street kids of New York as they struggle to survive after the events of House of M.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's comic adaptation of the classic teen mystery novel heroine Nancy Drew, updating the beloved detective character for a modern audience while preserving the cozy mystery appeal.

subject: series
synopsis: Anthony Del Col and Joe Eisma's dark revisionist thriller reimagining the teen detectives in a gritty noir where Nancy Drew and the Hardy Boys investigate adult crime with adult stakes.
author: Anthony Del Col

subject: series
synopsis: Survival thriller series from MadCave following characters trapped in a dangerous natural environment filled with predators and environmental hazards.

subject: series
synopsis: A Behemoth Comics series exploring fantasy adventure and epic quests.

subject: series
synopsis: Collected editions of Brian Michael Bendis's landmark New Avengers run, which assembled a new, more diverse team following the Avengers Disassembled event and redefined what an Avengers team could look like for a new generation of readers.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Matthew Rosenberg sends a team of New Mutants on supernatural investigation missions, building toward larger revelations while delivering effective horror-adjacent X-Men storytelling.

subject: series
synopsis: A time-travel miniseries pitting the original New Mutants against their future selves, written with nostalgic affection for the classic Claremont-era team.

synopsis: Chris Claremont reunites with the original New Mutants in a standalone story channeling the spirit of his original run, featuring Red Skull and alternate-reality intrigue.

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV and Alvaro Martinez Bueno's horror story about twelve friends at a luxury retreat who realise the house has sealed them in as the outside world ends.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: A monster-themed squad book following supernatural soldiers under Nick Fury, blending horror-movie creature tropes with classic war-comic structure for a fun genre mashup.

subject: series
synopsis: Sequel to Mark Millar's Night Club, continuing the story of a teenager who becomes a vampire and uses his powers as a superhero, blending YA sensibilities with Millar's action-oriented style.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series

author: Scott Snyder

subject: series
synopsis: A Behemoth Comics series blending fantasy with Shakespearean elements.

subject: series
synopsis: Eric Stephenson and Nate Bellegarde's sci-fi about four scientists who became celebrities — and what happened when their partnership fractured. The Beatles-of-science premise is clever.
author: Eric Stephenson

subject: series
synopsis: Shake-O's charming manga about a one-eyed school nurse who treats monster students with a variety of supernatural ailments, blending monster-of-the-week medical drama with warm character comedy.
author: Shake-O

subject: series
synopsis: A supernatural crime series from Dynamite featuring demonic characters navigating the criminal underworld, blending occult horror with neo-noir crime aesthetics.

subject: series

The strip's intelligence elevates it well above typical adult content.
author: Trudy Cooper

subject: series
synopsis: A deluxe edition collecting the first arc of Kieron Gillen and Dan Mora's acclaimed fantasy series, in which Arthurian legend resurfaces as a deadly modern threat.

subject: series
synopsis: Rich Burlew's stick-figure fantasy webcomic: a bumbling D&D adventuring party whose rules gags grow into an ambitious epic against the lich Xykon.

subject: series
synopsis: Masaaki Nakayama's Japanese horror manga consisting of interconnected stories about supernatural phenomena with roots in traumatic human behavior — presented with clinical detachment that makes the horror more insidious than any monster.
author: Masaaki Nakayama

subject: series
synopsis: Gerard Way and Shaun Simon's surreal comedy set in a home for people who may be alien abductees, following residents and staff through a series of escalating strange events. Way's experimental sensibility meets accessible humor in a distinctive premise.
author: Gerard Way

subject: series
synopsis: A Pathfinder tabletop-RPG tie-in mini from Dynamite pitting the game's heroes against an undead threat.

subject: series

subject: series

subject: series

subject: series

synopsis: A Boom/DC crossover in which the Green Lanterns and their power rings reach the Planet of the Apes.

subject: series
synopsis: Ryan Parrott's Boom series sending Jason, Zack and Trini into space as the Omega Rangers, companion to Mighty Morphin.

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: A heist-driven crime thriller in a near-future setting.

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: A Wildstorm comic tie-in to the Prototype video game, expanding on the world of Alex Mercer and the Blacklight virus.

subject: series
synopsis: A charming six-issue miniseries starring Pete Wisdom and Kitty Pryde as a couple navigating a spy thriller, written by Warren Ellis with sharp wit and his characteristic irreverence.

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Fialkov and Kody Chamberlain's satirical anthology comic strips various punk archetypes against absurdist comedy scenarios in a deliberately rough, sketch-comedy style.

subject: series
synopsis: Horror-comedy series featuring sinister supernatural cats wreaking havoc.
author: Erica Schultz

subject: series
synopsis: Volume of Queen Sonja, the spin-off series following Red Sonja as a ruling queen rather than a wandering warrior.

subject: series
synopsis: Saladin Ahmed's character study of Pietro Maximoff trapped in a time loop, examining his psychology and the cost of living faster than everyone around him.

subject: series

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Fred Duval and Emem's French SF series: in 2084, with Earth wrecked by climate change and conflict, an alien humanitarian federation arrives to intervene.

subject: series
synopsis: A Wildstorm series set in a post-alien invasion world following human resistance fighters.
author: Various

synopsis: Trade collections of Oni Press's Rick and Morty Presents one-shots, each spotlighting a supporting character from the show.

subject: series
synopsis: Post-apocalyptic action series about mercenaries navigating a shattered future.

synopsis: Tadatoshi Fujimaki's golf manga about Robo, an expressionless prodigy whose pinpoint 'laser beam' shots carry him up the amateur ranks.

synopsis: A six-issue limited series featuring a new vigilante character who becomes the driver-for-hire Rush City, written by Chuck Dixon with art by Tom Mandrake. Set in the DC universe but focusing on a street-level original character.

subject: series
synopsis: Pamela Ribon and Veronica Fish's roller-derby comic about two best friends who join a league and end up on rival teams.

subject: series
synopsis: A horror series from Zenescope drawing on urban legend and supernatural themes, featuring demonic forces threatening a small community.

subject: series
synopsis: A Wildstorm miniseries exploring the secret origin of Jack Hawksmoor, the God of Cities.

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Seeley's story of the time-displaced gladiator-warrior Shatterstar running a superhero temp agency while confronting questions of identity and free will.

subject: series
synopsis: A French bande dessinee science fiction series exploring isolation and community on a generation ship or isolated habitat — intimate in scale despite its cosmic setting, with strong humanist underpinning.

subject: series
synopsis: A late-1980s Marvel series in the tradition of the anthology horror and supernatural titles, featuring standalone tales of magic and the uncanny.

subject: series

synopsis: IDW crossover series pitting the G.I. Joe team against the Street Fighter roster in an action-packed tournament-style story.

synopsis: Garth Ennis's brutal six-issue western for Avatar Press, following an aging gunfighter navigating the death of the Old West as modernity encroaches on the frontier, with Ennis's characteristic unflinching violence and moral complexity.

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Carey's superhero deconstruction follows a cop who, after being nearly killed by a supervillain, makes a desperate choice to gain powers himself — exploring what drives ordinary people to the extremes of superheroism.
author: Mike Carey

subject: series
synopsis: Taiyo Matsumoto's lyrical series about children living in a group home, centered on the mystical power of a rusted old car — the 'Sunny' of the title — that becomes a vessel for dreams, memory, and escape. Among the most beautiful and emotionally resonant manga ever published.
author: Taiyo Matsumoto

subject: series
synopsis: Amanda Conner, Jimmy Palmiotti, and Rafael de Latorre's comedy about a teenage girl obsessed with superheroes who tries various methods to acquire powers, with the irreverent energy typical of Conner and Palmiotti's collaborations.

subject: series
synopsis: The classic ongoing series featuring Superboy (Clark Kent as a teenager) as a member of the Legion of Super-Heroes in the 30th century, serving as the Legion's flagship title through much of the 1970s and early 1980s.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis's Avatar miniseries positing that superheroes would function as literal gods — alien and incomprehensible to human values — depicting various nations' superhuman programs spiraling into apocalyptic disaster through Ellis's cynical, ideas-dense writing.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: A six-issue limited series by Neal Adams presenting a new threat involving multiple Supermen from Krypton and Apokolips forces threatening Earth. Adams' distinctive art style dominates this bombastic story.
author: Neal Adams

subject: series
synopsis: A reprint collection of the classic Superman newspaper comic strips from the late 1950s and 1960s, presenting the adventures of the Daily Planet team and Superman's rogues gallery in the clean Silver Age style.
author: Jerry Siegel

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore's continuation of his celebrated Supreme revamp through Awesome Entertainment, adapting the series for Image Comics when Awesome folded. Moore's love letter to Silver Age Superman remains compelling even in this transitional form.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Kevin Eastman, Peter Laird and Tom Waltz's dystopian future: the last surviving Turtle, alone in a militarized New York decades on, sets out to avenge his family.

subject: series
synopsis: A Loki/MCU-adjacent series exploring the Time Variance Authority's operations and mythology, benefiting from audience familiarity with the Disney+ series while expanding the temporal bureaucracy concept.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A Tank Girl miniseries by Alan Martin, continuing the anarchic adventures of the post-apocalyptic tank-driving punk antiheroine in the Australian outback. Carioca maintains the irreverent, chaotic energy of the original Hewlett/Martin run.
author: Alan Martin

subject: series
synopsis: A WWII-era story featuring the precursor to Team 7, a black ops unit in the Wildstorm universe.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: IDW all-ages comic tie-in to the Nickelodeon animated TMNT series, featuring the 2012 cartoon versions of the Turtles in new stories. Targeted at younger readers.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW prequel to The Last Ronin depicting what happened to the surviving Turtle in the years between the tragedy and the main story.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Milligan and Piotr Kowalski's Dynamite series follows a dying scientist whose experimental cancer treatment accidentally gives him devastating superpowers he uses to impose his darkening morality on others.
author: Peter Milligan

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore-plotted and Peter Hogan-scripted spinoff of Tom Strong featuring the alternate-Earth heroes of Terra Obscura. A solid Silver Age pastiche with genuine affection for the source material, though it lacks the density of Moore's primary ABC work.
author: Alan Moore, Peter Hogan

subject: series
synopsis: Terry Moore's sci-fi thriller about a photographer accidentally bonded to fragments of a military liquid metal suit. Moore's characterization and his willingness to slow down for human moments make this action thriller more substantial than its genre peers.
author: Terry Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Annual specials for the Adventures of Superman ongoing, featuring extended stories and crossover tie-ins during the post-Crisis Superman era when multiple Superman titles ran simultaneously.
author: Robert Loren Fleming

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar's superhero ensemble series exploring a team of international heroes assembled to address a global crisis, featuring Millar's signature high-concept action and world-building across multiple nations and hero archetypes.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: A post-Worldstorm Authority miniseries following the team's difficult reassembly and a new global threat.
author: Christos Gage

subject: series
synopsis: Jeremy Haun and Jason A. Hurley's horror thriller set in a world where a sexually transmitted disease makes its carriers strikingly beautiful — until they suddenly combust. Two detectives investigate what the disease really is and who is weaponizing it.
author: Jeremy Haun, Jason A. Hurley

subject: series
synopsis: Crime thriller series from MadCave exploring organ trafficking, black market body parts, or human trafficking in a gritty noir setting.
author: Zac Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Darick Robertson's Boys miniseries revealing Billy Butcher's complete origin — his childhood, his marriage, and the devastating event that set him on his path of revenge against superheroes.

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and John McCrea's Boys miniseries following Wee Hughie's return to Scotland to reconsider his life choices — a quieter character study in the midst of the main series' escalating chaos.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Tom DeFalco's three-issue MC2 mini in which Jack 'JJ' Jameson becomes the armored hero the Buzz, spun off from Spider-Girl.

subject: series
synopsis: An OGN volume in the Collected Toppi series showcasing Sergio Toppi's masterful work, here focusing on Japan — his precise, decorative linework applied to Japanese history and mythology with remarkable fidelity.
author: Sergio Toppi

subject: series
synopsis: Fred Van Lente and Ryan Dunlavey's comprehensive illustrated history of the comics medium from its origins to the present day — informative, funny, and self-aware, covering everything from newspaper strips to manga to underground comix.
author: Fred Van Lente

subject: series
synopsis: A licensed anthology series expanding the mythology of James O'Barr's The Crow, featuring different characters who return from the dead driven by vengeance. The series continued the gothic revenge-fantasy tone of the original while introducing new protagonists and storylines.

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Dysart and Pop Mhan's six-issue Etrigan mini.

subject: series
synopsis: Howard Chaykin's deliberately provocative political satire set in a near-future America after a catastrophic terrorist attack, following a team of pardoned criminals assembled to prevent further chaos. Intentionally transgressive and abrasive — significant in craft but deeply uncomfortable in execution.
author: Howard Chaykin

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman and Ryan Bodenheim's dense, ambitious story of an aging man who strikes a deal with an ancient underground civilization to save his dying wife, interweaving WWII flashbacks with a present-day conspiracy. author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Sean Lewis and Hayden Sherman's dystopian thriller set in a fractured near-future America where a woman discovers an abandoned baby and two soldiers who become unlikely protectors as they cross a war-torn landscape. Raw, scratchy artwork reinforces the bleakness of the setting.
author: Sean Lewis

subject: series
synopsis: The newer Ghost in the Shell manga following Major Kusanagi and Section 9 through cybercrime investigations in an updated version of the classic world. Competent continuation for fans of the franchise.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A masked vigilante whose power is literally a gimmick — a single trick device — navigates a superhero world that has moved on. Ahoy's satirical take on superhero obsolescence and reinvention.

subject: series
synopsis: A graphic novel adaptation of F. Scott Fitzgerald's classic American novel, translating the Jazz Age tragedy of Jay Gatsby's obsessive pursuit of Daisy Buchanan and the hollowness of the American Dream into sequential art form.
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

subject: series
synopsis: The original six-issue series by Steve Skeates and Steve Ditko introducing the contrasting super-brothers Hank and Don Hall as the violent Hawk and the pacifist Dove, making an allegorical statement about societal conflict during the late 1960s.
author: Steve Skeates

subject: series
synopsis: The second volume of G. Willow Wilson's acclaimed fantasy series about warring factions of humans and monsters who must forge an uneasy alliance.
author: G. Willow Wilson

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Starlin's follow-up to Infinity War, pitting Earth's heroes against the cosmic Goddess and her crusade to purge the universe of evil through destruction; notable for its large cast and philosophical religious themes, though considered somewhat lesser than its predecessors.
author: Jim Starlin

subject: series
synopsis: AWA's satirical take on suburban conformity and the American Dream, following a family with dangerous secrets behind their perfect facade. Genre blends domestic drama with dark thriller elements.

subject: series
synopsis: A manga adaptation of SNK's long-running fighting game franchise The King of Fighters, covering the plot of KOF XIV with new story material. Fan service for the fighting game community that expands on the game's storyline and gives more depth to the cast.
author: Kyotaro Azuma

subject: series
synopsis: S. Steven Struble and Sina Grace's sweet, melancholy slice-of-life comic about a ragdoll figure navigating young adult life — dating, friendships, music — with gentle humor and genuine emotional resonance. One of Image's best indie-flavored offerings with a devoted cult following.

subject: series
synopsis: A charming digital-first Infinity Comic spotlighting Lockheed, Kitty Pryde's alien dragon companion, in whimsical self-contained adventures.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Wood's post-collapse eco-thriller: the crew of the activist trawler Kapital roams a ruined world's oceans searching for its missing sister ship, The Massive.

subject: series
synopsis: Bryan J.L. Glass and Michael Avon Oeming's epic fantasy following a young mouse who becomes entangled in an ancient war between warrior orders, drawing on mythology and religion while building a richly detailed world. A genuine epic fantasy for comics readers who loved Bone or Mouse Guard.
author: Bryan J.L. Glass

subject: series
synopsis: A sword-and-sorcery anthology series from Ablaze featuring various barbarian warrior stories in the pulp fantasy tradition.

subject: series
synopsis: An all-ages fantasy adventure in which anthropomorphic animal warriors representing the Chinese zodiac must unite to protect the world from an ancient darkness.
author: J. Torres

subject: series
synopsis: A grieving couple ventures into a fantastical afterlife realm to rescue their daughter's soul.
author: Daniel Warren Johnson

subject: series
synopsis: Faith Erin Hicks' middle-grade fantasy trilogy set in a city that has been conquered and renamed so many times it is simply called The Nameless City, following a young monk-in-training and a street child as they navigate political upheaval and forge an unlikely friendship. author: Faith Erin Hicks

subject: series
synopsis: DC Comics' six-issue limited series adapting Star Trek: The Next Generation at the launch of the DC license in 1989, introducing comic readers to Picard's crew and establishing the visual and tonal approach DC would use for the subsequent ongoing series.

author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: A family discovers they are actually background characters in a video game world when the simulation begins to break down around them. Adam Glass's high-concept horror-comedy plays with questions of free will and existence within a reality-bending framework.
author: Adam Glass

subject: series
synopsis: A time-travel thriller following an assassin who travels through history to prevent disasters, only to discover that his missions may be creating the problems he was sent to solve. A compact, twisty series from Aftershock's early catalog.
author: Frank Barbiere

subject: series
synopsis: Erwann Surcouf's French post-apocalyptic adventure in which bands of hunters roam a ruined world overrun by giant beasts.

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover series pairing two of fiction's most iconic dark vigilantes: DC's Batman and the classic pulp hero The Shadow, spanning their respective eras and uniting them against a shared threat.

subject: series
synopsis: A modern-day sequel to Dynamite's Shadow comics placing the classic pulp vigilante in the contemporary era, exploring how a creature of the 1930s adapts to 21st-century crime.

subject: series
synopsis: Hajime Kanzaka's comedic fantasy stars Lina Inverse, a brilliant, short-tempered teenage sorceress whose appetite for treasure and destruction leaves devastation in her wake. A fast, irreverent sword-and-sorcery romp.
author: Hajime Kanzaka

subject: series
synopsis: Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa adapts the climactic final third of Stephen King's The Stand with fidelity to King's apocalyptic vision, featuring Mike Perkins' atmospheric painted art.
author: Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa

subject: series

author: Chuck Hogan, Guillermo del Toro

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jolley and Jamal Igle's Terminator miniseries set in 1992, following a mercenary who gets caught between Skynet's machines and a resistance fighter while an unexpected target becomes central to both factions. Solid licensed thriller work.
author: Dan Jolley

subject: series
synopsis: Free Comic Book Day special issues featuring Ben Edlund's satirical superhero The Tick, distributed as promotional material at participating comic shops over multiple years.

subject: series
synopsis: A Tick miniseries from 1999 featuring Ben Edlund's satirical blue superhero in extended city-spanning adventures, continuing the absurdist superhero parody tradition of the original series.

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak returns to the Hulk mythos with Amadeus Cho taking the mantle from Bruce Banner, bringing a lighter, more optimistic tone to the Hulk concept while exploring what it means to be a hero who actually enjoys his power.
author: Greg Pak

subject: series
synopsis: A European comics series exploring division — physical, political, or social — through the metaphor of a wall separating communities or peoples, with strong allegorical resonance.

subject: series
synopsis: Edward Laroche's science fiction thriller about a future Earth where a classified government agency monitors alien incursion, focusing on soldiers equipped with extraordinary technology facing an existential threat. Dense military sci-fi with ambitious scope.
author: Edward Laroche

subject: series
synopsis: Spin-off graphic novel series set at Mouseford Academy, following the Thea Sisters through school-based adventures and friendships.

subject: series
synopsis: Eric Stephenson and Simon Gane's thriller about a secret society of people with special abilities who operate outside normal society under the enigmatic Voice, exploring whether powers make you better than ordinary humans or simply more dangerous. author: Eric Stephenson

subject: series
synopsis: Modern Thor relaunch blending mythology with contemporary themes.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: The second volume of Dynamite's crime-thriller Uncanny, featuring a man with the ability to copy any skill he touches, navigating a dangerous underworld of criminals and conspiracies.

synopsis: A miniseries in the Grimm Fairy Tales universe pitting the female Van Helsing against Frankenstein's monster, blending classic monster-hunting action with Zenescope's mature, action-heavy style.

subject: series
synopsis: A quirky miniseries featuring the Teen Brigade and the Antithesis, with a satirical take on superhero legacies and the nature of heroism that leans into absurdist humor.
